text: i18n: UI strings are English-only; no localization layer

Part 1/3 landed in 42bc831: the web i18n layer (locales.ts, messages/en.ts, index.tsx with I18nProvider/useT), wired at the app root, plus a first tranche of migrated strings. Ships English only. Two decisions worth knowing for the rest of the work: (1) the context default is functional rather than null, so useT works outside a provider and components stay unit-testable as isolated subtrees, while setLocale throws because that IS a real bug — this avoided wrapping all nine existing page tests and every future one; (2) pure functions like formatLastSeen take t as a parameter rather than reaching for a hook, which is what keeps their tests able to assert exact wording. Also: localStorage persistence of the chosen locale ended up in the provider rather than in T-127, since that is where the locale state lives and splitting it would have meant touching the provider twice — T-127 is now purely the two UI surfaces. Remaining: ~150 more web strings (concentrated in ListPropsPage, ItemDialog, SettingsPage, LoginPage), then the Android layer and its ~205 strings.

Parts 2-3 landed (7862a0d, 5dd5bd3): LoginPage, RedeemPage, SyncIndicator, ItemDialog, ListPropsPage migrated; syncStatus and relativeTime now share one set of ago.* keys rather than carrying identical copies of the same four labels. Android decision made rather than deferred: CompositionLocalProvider with a localized Context, NOT AppCompatDelegate.setApplicationLocales. Reasons — it yields LocalLayoutDirection, which is exactly the hook T-126 needs for Arabic, and it avoids dragging the AppCompat theming stack into a pure Compose/Material3 app. Its one real gap is strings resolved outside composition (the collaborator-change notification poster), to be closed explicitly with a localized-context helper rather than ignored. Accepted cost: no integration with Android's system per-app-language screen, which matters little for an APK-distributed self-hosted app. Remaining: SettingsPage/AdminPage/OverviewPage/ListPage leftovers (~30 web strings), then the Android layer and its ~205 strings.

Part 5 (a4b4725): Android layer built and the composable screens migrated — 172 strings in strings.xml, no <plurals> anywhere. Android decision implemented as planned: CompositionLocalProvider over LocalContext/LocalConfiguration/LocalLayoutDirection, no appcompat. One implementation detail that matters: LocalContext must be overridden, not just LocalConfiguration — stringResource resolves against the context's resources, so providing only the configuration would flip layout direction while leaving every string in the system language. Compiler caught three sites where stringResource had to be hoisted rather than substituted (inside a LaunchedEffect coroutine and inside a semantics lambda — neither is a composition), and surfaced two strings the extraction sweep had missed because they start with an interpolation rather than a capital. Remaining: SettingsScreen (~40), ListPropsScreen (~32) and SyncStatusBar (~12) composables; the six ViewModels' messages via UiText (Settings 25, Admin 9, Login 8, ListProps 9, ItemForm 5, Redeem 3); the notification poster via localizedContext; and LastSeen/formatBackgroundSync onto resources.

Done across six commits (42bc831, 7862a0d, 5dd5bd3, fed36b3, a4b4725, f20793d). Both clients fully extracted; English only. Design notes that matter for the tickets that depend on this: (1) NO plural machinery anywhere on either client — T-123 earned that, and it is why Ukrainian (3 forms) and Arabic (6) cost nothing beyond translation. (2) Pure functions take the resolver rather than reaching for a hook — web passes t, Android returns UiText — which is what kept SyncStatusBarTest and LastSeenTest free of Robolectric and the web equivalents free of a provider. (3) UiText args can nest, so composed messages ('Synced {ago}') keep both halves independently translatable instead of being concatenated at the call site. (4) Server-supplied error text stays UiText.Raw and untranslated on Android / err.message on web — the server has no i18n, and fixing that properly means mapping the wire contract's error CODES client-side. Worth its own ticket if it matters. (5) The compiler caught seven sites where a string had to be hoisted out of a coroutine or a semantics lambda, or a helper made @Composable; a test run would have caught none of them. T-126 (RTL), T-127 (chooser) and T-124 (translations) are now unblocked.
